Gothic-Slavic Essentialism and Cultural Conflict
Your objection—that characterizing the Goths as a doomed "smaller ruling elite" and predicting their absorption smacks of cultural fatalism and essentialism when they constitute nearly half the population of the Bohemian basin—is a crucial point that compels a re-evaluation of the long-term political forecast, drawing directly on the dynamics detailed in the sources regarding the interplay between Germanic and Slavic peoples.
You are correct that the Goths represent a powerful demographic force at near parity with the proto-West Slavs (45,000 Goths to 45,000 Slavs, per the scenario), making the prediction of their eventual cultural absorption difficult to sustain solely based on the historical precedent of a much smaller conqueror being absorbed [Previous response].
However, the sources illustrate why the political and cultural structures that these two parity populations embody—even with a Romanized, tolerant Gothic administration—create a fatal collision course rooted in opposing social structures.
The Conflict of Cultural Essentialism
The sources inherently frame the history of this region in terms of essential, unresolvable cultural conflict, which justifies the previously predicted outcome, regardless of population figures.
1. Fundamental Political Difference: The Gothic polity, though highly Romanized and focused on legalism, local autonomy, and tolerance [Previous response], is fundamentally defined by the presence of "privileged castes" [1]. The Goths maintain a warrior aristocracy, reserving the "labours of war" for themselves [Previous response]. This system, which aims to unite the vigour of Germany and the culture of Rome [Previous response], is antithetical to the core nature of the indigenous population. The proto-West Slavs (Czekhes and Moravians) are characterized as "purely democratic" in their fundamental elements, industrious, and living in patriarchal communities [1]. The conflict between the aristocratic Gothic structure and the democratic Slavic character is deemed the "principal idea and fundamental feature of Bohemian history,"expressed as the "uninterrupted clashing and struggle of Slavism and Germanism" [2]. This struggle is inevitable because the Goths' culture is one of warlike, conquering, oppressing all their neighbours, while the Slavs are peaceful [1].
2. The Persistence of Slavic Identity: The Goths, despite being half the population, are still introducing a foreign system. Historically, the Western Slavs, particularly the Chekhs of Bohemia, have demonstrated an immense determination to preserve their historical identity [3]. They regained their numbers and maintained their identity despite being reduced from three million to eight hundred thousand following centuries of strife [3, 4]. This demonstrates a powerful cultural and demographic resilience against external pressure. Furthermore, the Slavs were deeply protective of their vernacular language in religious and civil affairs, often resisting the imposition of foreign languages, which suggests an enduring mechanism for maintaining cultural distinction [Previous response].
3. The Vulnerability of the Conqueror: Even in cases where the two groups are numerically disparate, the sources note that the conquering nationality may be merged into that of the natives, leaving behind primarily a warlike spirit[Previous response]. While this scenario presents population parity, the Goths are entering a new environment after an epic flight from Justinian [Scenario], having lost their established homeland and legitimacy in Italy. They bring with them the administrative experience of Rome but lack the deep, organic roots of the indigenous Slavs in the Bohemian basin.
Cultural Identity Over Population Numbers
The success of the Romanized Gothic state relies on the Slavs accepting their designated role as the "trading and labouring caste" [Previous response] under a tolerant legal system. However, the democratic and communal Slavic nature makes them resistant to this political and social subjugation, irrespective of their numbers relative to the Goths.
The sheer mass of the Slavs (45,000 individuals belonging to races like the Bohemians and Moravians [5], who belong to the Northwest Slavic stem [6]) ensures that the Goths cannot rely on demographic control. The resultant polity, therefore, must choose between absorption of the Gothic elite or perpetual conflict. Given the Slavs' historical track record of overcoming Germanizing influences [3, 4, 7, 8], the predicted fatalism of absorption reflects the power of Slavism's democratic essentialism against the Germanic/Gothic essentialism of privileged, military caste rule [1].

Gothic Legalism and Slavic Resistance
Your hypothesis that these highly Romanized Goths would establish a state based on legalism, local autonomy, and tolerance of a multilingual, multiethnic body politic aligns strongly with the theoretical ideals and administrative precedents established by the Ostrogothic monarchy, particularly during its period of stability in Ravenna.
This approach would be highly successful in creating an organized, multi-layered administration, but it would not eliminate the deep political friction arising from the fundamental character differences between the Goths and the proto-West Slavs.
Foundation in Legalism and Tolerance (Civilitas)
The establishment of a state founded on legalism and tolerance is entirely consistent with the Gothic experience and philosophy, despite their ultimate military objective.
1. Observance of Law (Civilitas): The Gothic political ideal, championed by rulers like Theoderic, was the strict observance of "CIVILITAS" (law and order) [1]. The Goths believed that the "true mark of civilitas is the observance of law" and that this is what separates man from beasts [2]. The Gothic sovereigns under this model were "exceedingly careful to observe justice" and preserved "the laws on a sure basis" [3]. The Goths aimed to ensure that their rule adhered to the legislation of Antiquity [4].
2. Religious Tolerance: A policy of religious tolerance would be maintained. The Goths were Arians, but their historical policy was one of profound non-interference in religious practice. Theoderic was an "Arian of the most tolerant description" [5], ensuring that Italians were not forced to change their belief and that the sanctuaries of the Romans received "the highest honour" [6, 7]. Extending this tolerance to the indigenous pagan Slavs would be a rational continuation of policy, aimed at political stability rather than dangerous proselytization [6].
3. Multilingual and Multiethnic Body Politic: The Romanized Goths, having suffered the destabilizing effects of warfare with Justinian, would prioritize peace and governance. The stated Gothic goal was that "Goths and Romans shall meet with impartial treatment at our hands", with the only division being that Goths carry out the "labours of war" while Romans (and by extension, the subjugated population) increase their numbers through "peaceable inhabitancy" [8, 9]. This legal framework explicitly supports a dual state, the Gothorum Romanorumque Rex [10].
Local Autonomy and Slavic Culture
By choosing not to impose Gothic or Latin as universal languages, the Romanized Goths avoid the key flashpoint that later plagued German-Slavic relations, allowing a degree of effective local autonomy.
1. Retention of Local Leadership and Law: Following the Ostrogothic model, the Goths would maintain local administration. In Italy, Romans were allowed to hold all state offices [7]. In Bohemia, the Slavs, divided into several tribes speaking "different dialects" [11, 12], could retain their local chiefs, the Knes, Zupan [11], and their established local judicial systems. This is an application of the Goths' administrative preference for adapting Roman civil institutions.
2. Slavic Cultural Expression: The polity's tolerance would allow the native Slavic culture to flourish outside the military and high governmental sphere. The earliest traces of Czekhish/Bohemian literature were often popular songs preserved only by tradition [13]. The Slavs were noted for their early fondness for music and poetry [14], and this vibrant, indigenous culture could continue to develop, albeit potentially under the pervasive, if subtle, influence of the Gothic ruling elite.
3. Linguistic Status: While Gothic is maintained as the elite or military tongue, the Slavs are left to use their various local dialects. This choice avoids the "obstinate resistance" that historically occurred when Germanic converters demanded the "sacrifice of their language, their customs, their whole nationality" [15]. It also avoids the specific historical trigger of the Bohemians rebelling when the Latin tongue was employed in divine worship [16].

Even with tolerance and legalism, the structure of the Gothic state remains fundamentally at odds with the nature of the indigenous population, guaranteeing a defining cultural and political struggle.
• Aristocracy vs. Democracy: The Goths impose a system containing the "germs of privileged castes" (the warrior elite) [17]. This is inherently contradictory to the fundamental character of the Slavs, who are "purely democratic" [17], a fact that forms the principal feature of the region's history: the "uninterrupted clashing and struggle of Slavism and Germanism" [18].
• Warlike vs. Peaceful Identity: The Goths, highly militarized and steeped in a warlike spirit [19], would govern a population described as naturally peaceful and industrious[17]. The Goths require the latter to serve as the tax-paying, laboring class [20], while reserving the status of the "valiant men" for themselves [21].
• The Unavoidable Outcome: Although the Goths' organizational superiority [22] would ensure they establish this legalistic state initially, the historical pattern among the Slavs is that a smaller conquering nationality is often absorbed by the natives, retaining only the injected warlike spirit [23]. The Gothic political rigidity, despite its civilized approach, is therefore set up for long-term cultural erosion against the resilience and numerical strength of the Slavic population. Evolution of the Gothic-Slavic Koine, 6th-10th Centuries
Your query posits that over three centuries (from the mid-6th century to 900 CE), the Gothic-Slavic Koine would evolve dramatically beyond its initial function as a limited contact language, driven by mixed families, market realities, and administrative necessities. The sources strongly support this transformation, emphasizing that these functional demands created a self-reinforcing linguistic network that guaranteed the Koine's endurance and dominance in public life, actively challenging the sources' own predictions of cultural stagnation [1-3].
By 900 CE, the linguistic landscape was indeed altered, moving the Koine toward a state of functional cohesion that placed it at the center of the dynamic, unified Gothic-Slavic polity [1, 3].
I. Koine's Initial Limitation vs. Its Functional Expansion
The sources affirm that the Koine was initially designed to be limited, but its function was so vital to the state's survival that it necessarily spread throughout the essential domains of society [4, 5]:
• Initial Limitation: The Koine was explicitly designed to operate between the castes [6-8], defined as a "functional language" [8-11] for military and administrative spheres [4, 5, 12]. The Goths maintained Gothic as the language of "sacred status" [8, 13-15] and the Slavs fiercely maintained their local dialects (řeč) for "domestic use, poetry, and cultural expression" [6-8, 11, 16]. This linguistic segregation was intended to prevent the Koine from developing into a full creole [6, 8-10].
• Expansion by Necessity: Despite this intended limitation, the Koine became the structural "cement" of the state [17], guaranteed a "very strong, lasting place" in the Bohemian basin due to the "constant demand for defensive readiness" against the Avars and Byzantium [2, 18-21], and economic interdependence [2, 22, 23].
II. Market and Urban Realities Drive Linguistic Fusion
The most significant shift came through the economy and urbanization, where the Koine transitioned from a language of momentary contact to a daily, necessary tool for the majority population [22, 24].
1. Urban Centers and Mixed Families
Urban administrative centers (Grads) became "natural targets for settlement by mixed families and merchants,"which actively reinforced linguistic fusion at the local level [2, 22, 24, 25].
• Linguistic Environment: Mixed families, such as the Gothic administrator Wulfaric and the Slavic merchant Svatava, raised children in a bilingual urban environment [26]. The Koine, being the shared public language, became the "language of opportunity" for the children, setting the stage for it to become a full creole language within a few generations [27-29].
• Commercial Language: The Koine served as the "indispensable market language" [24, 30-33] for the Slavs, who were the "trading and labouring caste" [2, 22, 24, 34, 35]. This meant that commercial transactions (Obchod), quick bargaining, and logistical exchanges were conducted entirely in the Koine, ensuring its daily reinforcement [33, 36, 37].
• Literacy Spread: The market demand provided functional literacy in the Koine to the Slavs, who needed to handle the bureaucratic logistics of taxes (Terna) and quotas (Numerus) [2, 24, 30, 31, 38]. This required the new generation to be trained in the Koine and administrative arithmetic, primarily in schools attached to convents in the Grads [39].
2. Lexical and Grammatical Transformation
Over 300 years, the Koine developed its own stable, simplified grammar, distinct from its parent languages [40, 41].
• Radical Simplification: The Koine underwent "radical grammatical simplification" [2, 18, 41], largely abandoning the complex case systems of both Slavic (seven cases in the singular) and Gothic, replacing them with prepositions and fixed word order for clarity [41-43]. This efficiency made it easier and more convenient than the highly inflected parent languages for public communication [44, 45].
• Syncretic Vocabulary: The language fused high-status Gothic/Latin terms (e.g., Imperativ, Sihu, Comes) for command and administration with Slavic terms for local life and goods (e.g., Zemlja, Vojak, Chléb) [46-48]. This lexical split codified the functional nature of the language, but the infusion of Gothic terms into Slavic discussions about warfare or politics [44, 49] demonstrated a deep influence [44, 49].
III. Administrative and Military Realities Deepen the Shift
The demands of the Gothic state structure guaranteed the Koine's social mobility and widespread geographical presence [2, 50].
1. Structural Permeability
The Gothic system maintained the loyalty of the ambitious indigenous elite through Structural Permeability, making Koine mastery synonymous with advancement [2, 51, 52].
• Meritocracy: The Goths prized "merit" and "eloquence and learning" [51-53]. For Slavs in the periphery, mastering the Koine provided access to the structured career path of service (militia), leading to administrative status and honors like Spectabilis and Illustris [2, 51, 53, 54]. This meant that cooperation (and Koine usage) led to power, actively undercutting the ideological clash [3, 51, 55].
• Intermediaries: Slavic local chiefs (Knes, Zupan) were "incorporated as subordinate civil administrators and military commanders" [2, 51, 53, 54, 56]. Their ability to receive Gothic commands (Imperativ) and relay demands (Numerus) relied entirely on the Koine, ensuring that the language of central administration penetrated every village with a local leader [57, 58].
2. Geographical and Structural Dominance
The Koine became the only language that successfully operated across the entire multiethnic, geographically expanded realm [59].
• Transcending Dialects: The Koine provided a neutral, standardized linguistic platform for administrative and military communication that transcended the existing "different dialects" (řeč) spoken by the kindred Slavic tribes (Czekhes, Moravians, Slovaks, Sorabians) [59].
• Fixed Network: The constant military threat guaranteed the Koine a "very strong, lasting place" by securing communication networks for military logistics and chancery records across the expansive borders [2, 21, 57]. As the "only literate society in the area" [6], the Gothic administration relied on the Koine's written form for functional use (taxes, quotas, commands), utilizing a simplified script imposed by the ruling elite [60, 61].
Therefore, by 900 CE, the Koine had fundamentally changed the linguistic landscape: it was no longer merely a border language, but the permanent, adaptable administrative backbone and the language of social mobility for a dynamically unified polity [1, 62, 63].

Gothic-Slavic Koine: Dominance and Functional Limits by 900 CE
Your hypothesis—that by 900 CE the Gothic-Slavic Koine would have reached a critical stage where its native speakers (L1 users) outnumbered the Goths, and that it would be more widespread geographically than either parent language—is strongly supported by the functional and structural realities of the polity, despite the sources’ insistence on cultural segregation [1-4].
The Koine's ubiquity in all essential, centralized spheres of life guaranteed its demographic and geographic dominance [5-7].
I. Koine Dominance in Speakers and Geography (900 CE)
By 900 CE, after over three centuries of existence, the Koine's role as the indispensable tool of administration, military command, and trade across the expanded state would make it the most widely spoken language functionally, and place it firmly on the path to becoming a full creole [4, 5, 8].
1. Koine Speakers Outnumbering Goths
The Koine was the mandatory language for functional interaction between the Gothic superstrate and the Slavic substrate [6, 7, 9]. Given the rigid segregation of the parent languages, any individual engaging in public life had to use the Koine, dramatically expanding its speaker base beyond the Gothic elite:
• Slavic Intermediaries: Slavic leaders (Knes, Zupan) were "incorporated as subordinate civil administrators and military commanders" [2, 5, 10]. They had to master the Koine to communicate state demands (Numerus, Terna) to the local populace and receive commands from the Gothic elite [2, 10-12]. This entire class—essential for state function—spoke the Koine by necessity.
• Literate Mercantile Class: The Slavs, as the "trading and labouring caste," required the Koine for the lucrative Vibrant Trade economy centered in the urban Grads [5, 11, 13, 14]. The market demand for the Koine provided "functional literacy" to a vast number of Slavic merchants [11, 15, 16]. This class, which includes mixed families and ambitious individuals, relied on the Koine daily for commerce (Obchod), transactions, and logistics [5, 11, 14, 17, 18].
• Military Auxiliaries: The Koine functioned as the lingua militaris for "rapid and clear coordination" of mixed forces, integrating Slavic Foederati into the Gothic command structure [5, 7, 9, 19]. The Koine was literally the language of survival for all troops standing "shoulder-to-shoulder" [9, 19].
• The Rise of Native Speakers (Creolization): The Koine became the "language of opportunity" for the children of mixed families and upwardly mobile Slavic merchants who settled in the Grads [5, 18, 20]. This constant use of the Koine, particularly in urban settings, set the stage for it to become a "full creole language" [5, 8, 20, 21]. Once Koine-speaking children began using it as their first language, its native speaker base would grow rapidly, eventually outnumbering the original Gothic population (45,000 individuals) [22].
2. Koine as the Geographically Most Widespread Language
The Koine, being the official language of the centralized, literate state administration, covered the entire operational territory of the expanded kingdom [7, 23].
• Communication Networks: The Koine standardized chancery documents (for taxes and quotas) and military logistics across the realm [5, 15, 17, 24]. This guaranteed its presence in every administrative center, frontier garrison, and trade node across the Bohemian basin, Moravia, and the incorporated kindred Slavic regions [23, 25].
• Transcendence of Dialects: The Slavic substrate was fragmented into "different dialects" (řeč) [2, 26]. The Koine provided a neutral, standardized linguistic platform that transcended these local differences, ensuring efficient administration and military cohesion among diverse kindred groups (Czekhes, Moravians, Slovaks, Sorabians) [2, 10].
• External Reach: The Koine, as the "indispensable market language," would have extended its geographical reach beyond the official borders into neighboring polities for cross-border commerce [7, 14]. This simplified tongue facilitated transactions with neighboring, often illiterate, polities [7].
II. The Sources' Caveat: Cultural Resistance Remains
While functional necessity ensured the Koine's demographic and geographic spread, the sources maintain that the parent languages survived culturally, confirming that the Koine remained fundamentally a functional language [2, 4].
• Gothic (Sacred Status): The Gothic elite intentionally maintained Gothic (the language of the Wulfila Bible) for their own internal affairs, upholding its "sacred status" [1, 4, 27]. This prevented the Koine from penetrating the highest echelons of Arian religious culture and high command [28].
• Slavic Dialects (řeč) (Domestic Culture): The Goths followed a policy of tolerance, allowing the Slavs to "maintain their local dialects (řeč)" for "domestic use, poetry, and cultural expression" [1, 4, 29, 30]. The Slavs showed an "immense determination to preserve their historical identity" [1]. This active preservation of řečensured that while the Koine dominated public life, the Slavic vernacular remained the language of the home and cultural resilience [4, 29].
• Koine's Functional Limitation: The Koine was explicitly defined as a "functional language" designed to operate between the castes, not to "supplant these core linguistic identities" [1, 4]. This structural choice prevented the Koine from developing into a native literature or achieving sacred status [4, 24, 28].

Your assessment that the stability mechanisms established by the Gothic administration would lead to a dynamic, unified, and self-reinforcing polity by 900 CE is fully supported by prioritizing the state’s organizational superiority and functional necessity over the sources’ deterministic cultural biases [1-3].
By 900 CE, after over three centuries of existence, the Gothic-Slavic realm would stand as the formidable organized power in Central Europe, enjoying a degree of unity and administrative capacity that centuries surpassed its fragmented neighbors [4].
This dynamic unity was achieved and sustained through self-reinforcing mechanisms in governance, military integration, and economic dependence.
I. Self-Reinforcing Unity through Organizational Superiority
The Gothic state’s endurance into the 10th century was rooted in its highly developed Romanized statecraft, which provided stability unmatched in the surrounding region.
1. Legal and Administrative Cohesion: The polity operated on principles that guaranteed consistency and order [5]. The Goths adhered strictly to "CIVILITAS" (observance of law and order) and aimed to follow the "legislation of Antiquity" [5, 6]. The retention of sophisticated administrative functions—such as the Praetorian Praefect [5], Quaestor, and Comes Sacrarum Largitionum [7]—ensured that the state could manage complex logistical and fiscal demands across its expanded borders [6, 8].

This approach would be highly successful in creating an organized, multi-layered administration, but it would not eliminate the deep political friction arising from the fundamental character differences between the Goths and the proto-West Slavs.
Foundation in Legalism and Tolerance (Civilitas)
The establishment of a state founded on legalism and tolerance is entirely consistent with the Gothic experience and philosophy, despite their ultimate military objective.
1. Observance of Law (Civilitas): The Gothic political ideal, championed by rulers like Theoderic, was the strict observance of "CIVILITAS" (law and order) [1]. The Goths believed that the "true mark of civilitas is the observance of law" and that this is what separates man from beasts [2]. The Gothic sovereigns under this model were "exceedingly careful to observe justice" and preserved "the laws on a sure basis" [3]. The Goths aimed to ensure that their rule adhered to the legislation of Antiquity [4].
2. Religious Tolerance: A policy of religious tolerance would be maintained. The Goths were Arians, but their historical policy was one of profound non-interference in religious practice. Theoderic was an "Arian of the most tolerant description" [5], ensuring that Italians were not forced to change their belief and that the sanctuaries of the Romans received "the highest honour" [6, 7]. Extending this tolerance to the indigenous pagan Slavs would be a rational continuation of policy, aimed at political stability rather than dangerous proselytization [6].
3. Multilingual and Multiethnic Body Politic: The Romanized Goths, having suffered the destabilizing effects of warfare with Justinian, would prioritize peace and governance. The stated Gothic goal was that "Goths and Romans shall meet with impartial treatment at our hands", with the only division being that Goths carry out the "labours of war" while Romans (and by extension, the subjugated population) increase their numbers through "peaceable inhabitancy" [8, 9]. This legal framework explicitly supports a dual state, the Gothorum Romanorumque Rex [10].
Local Autonomy and Slavic Culture
By choosing not to impose Gothic or Latin as universal languages, the Romanized Goths avoid the key flashpoint that later plagued German-Slavic relations, allowing a degree of effective local autonomy.
1. Retention of Local Leadership and Law: Following the Ostrogothic model, the Goths would maintain local administration. In Italy, Romans were allowed to hold all state offices [7]. In Bohemia, the Slavs, divided into several tribes speaking "different dialects" [11, 12], could retain their local chiefs, the Knes, Zupan [11], and their established local judicial systems. This is an application of the Goths' administrative preference for adapting Roman civil institutions.
2. Slavic Cultural Expression: The polity's tolerance would allow the native Slavic culture to flourish outside the military and high governmental sphere. The earliest traces of Czekhish/Bohemian literature were often popular songs preserved only by tradition [13]. The Slavs were noted for their early fondness for music and poetry [14], and this vibrant, indigenous culture could continue to develop, albeit potentially under the pervasive, if subtle, influence of the Gothic ruling elite.
3. Linguistic Status: While Gothic is maintained as the elite or military tongue, the Slavs are left to use their various local dialects. This choice avoids the "obstinate resistance" that historically occurred when Germanic converters demanded the "sacrifice of their language, their customs, their whole nationality" [15]. It also avoids the specific historical trigger of the Bohemians rebelling when the Latin tongue was employed in divine worship [16].
Inherent Conflict Despite Tolerance
Even with tolerance and legalism, the structure of the Gothic state remains fundamentally at odds with the nature of the indigenous population, guaranteeing a defining cultural and political struggle.
• Aristocracy vs. Democracy: The Goths impose a system containing the "germs of privileged castes" (the warrior elite) [17]. This is inherently contradictory to the fundamental character of the Slavs, who are "purely democratic" [17], a fact that forms the principal feature of the region's history: the "uninterrupted clashing and struggle of Slavism and Germanism" [18].
• Warlike vs. Peaceful Identity: The Goths, highly militarized and steeped in a warlike spirit [19], would govern a population described as naturally peaceful and industrious[17]. The Goths require the latter to serve as the tax-paying, laboring class [20], while reserving the status of the "valiant men" for themselves [21].
• The Unavoidable Outcome: Although the Goths' organizational superiority [22] would ensure they establish this legalistic state initially, the historical pattern among the Slavs is that a smaller conquering nationality is often absorbed by the natives, retaining only the injected warlike spirit [23]. The Gothic political rigidity, despite its civilized approach, is therefore set up for long-term cultural erosion against the resilience and numerical strength of the Slavic population. The state would succeed as a legal administration, but fail as a monolithic cultural entity.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Gothic Rule Over Slavs: A Hypothetical Failure
The hypothetical Gothic polity, highly Romanized and possessing organizational superiority, could achieve its short-term goal of reserving high functions and military control to the Gothic language and culture, while simultaneously permitting local Slavic autonomy. However, the plan to sustain this structure under an Arianized Slavic nobility would be critically challenged and likely fail long-term due to the deep-seated cultural characteristics of the proto-West Slavs.
Retention of Gothic in State, Cities, and Army
The Goths' organizational culture, honed by ruling from Ravenna, strongly supports the retention of Gothic and Latin for elite functions, military command, and high administration:
• Army and Elites: The Goths viewed themselves as the warrior caste [Previous response, 414]. They elected their leaders in an ancestral fashion upon a shield [461, Previous response], signifying the retention of Gothic tradition in military command. Their strength in numbers (near parity with the Slavs) and warlike spirit [9, Previous response] would ensure Gothic is the language of the army.
• State and Cities (Romanized Administration): The Goths would model their state on the Ostrogothic Kingdom, aiming to unite the vigour of Germany and the culture of Rome[Previous response].
    ◦ The Gothic ruler would bear a title signifying dual authority (e.g., 'King of Goths and Romans') [Previous response].
    ◦ Latin would likely be the language of bureaucracy and high law, as Romans famously continued to hold all the offices of the state in Italy [1].
    ◦ Gothic would be elevated to a sacred status due to the Wulfila Bible and the unique Gothic script [Previous response, 646, 714], ensuring its use in the ruling caste's worship and cultural sphere.
• Cities: Cities would be the primary centers of this Gothic/Latin administration, contrasting with the agrarian countryside. The populace of cities, historically in countries like Poland, consisted primarily of nobility and inhabitants of the cities (e.g., Poles of the Leckian race) [2], making them natural targets for Gothic/Latin administrative dominance.
Allowing Slavic Populace to "Do Their Own Thing"

AD USUM BELLICUM ET ADMINISTRATIVUM
MILITARY REPORT: STATE OF GARRISONS IN THE KRAJINA (THE MOUNTAIN RIM OF BOHEMIA) Circa Anno 700 P.C. (Post Christum)
TO: The Royal War Council (Consilium Militaris), Ravenna-on-ElbeFROM: The Office of the Comes of Frontier Logistics
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS PRAESENS: ADHERENCE TO CIVILITAS
The general status of the Gothic garrisons along the Bohemian mountain rim remains Hardus (strong/courageous) [1], maintained by the rigorous application of Romanized Civilitas (legal order/state governance) [2, 3]. Our kingdom endures as a great bulwark [4] against external pressures [5]. Despite the underlying uninterrupted clashing and struggle of Slavism and Germanism [6, 7], the administrative structures governing military operation remain firm [2]. We are the only literate society in the area [4, 8], affording us an immense advantage in intelligence and logistical management [4].
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. GARRISON DEPLOYMENT AND ORGANIZATION (Militia)
Gothic military forces remain focused on the borderlands, relying on our centralized organization and the necessity of military unity [5, 9].
1. Fortification and Control (Grads): The Gothic warrior caste [2, 9] maintains primary residency in the fortified cities (Grads) [10, 11], which serve as the seats of administration and the centers of trade (Obchod) [12, 13]. These locations are the operational hubs for troop deployment into the Krajina (region/borderland) [1].
2. Personnel Composition (Numerus): Garrison strength is primarily derived from the command structure of the Gothic elite and the auxiliary Slavic forces [9].
    ◦ Gothic Elite: High officers, the Comites (Commanders) [3, 9], utilize Gothic and Latin for recording official documents and high-level strategy, lending grace to the warrior nature [2].
    ◦ Slavic Auxiliaries (Foederati): The numerosity of the indigenous populace, the Czekhes and Moravians, is incorporated as Foederati (auxiliary troops) [1, 9]. These troops are led by their indigenous chiefs, the Zupani and Knes [1, 9], ensuring shared command and organization[9].
    ◦ Logistics: The census of troops and material (the Numerus) [2-4] is managed centrally, confirming the organizational superiority of the state against fragmented, illiterate tribal confederations [4].
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. FRONTIER COMMUNICATION AND LINGUISTIC STATUS
The state of readiness in the mountain rim is entirely dependent upon the functional efficiency of the Gothic-Slavic Koine (lingua militaris) [9].
1. Koine as Imperativ: The Koine, being radically simplified [14], ensures that imperative commands [3, 4] are unambiguous despite the multiethnic composition of the army [2].
2. Operational Lexicon: Routine frontier tasks utilize a mixed lexicon drawn from the Koine Glossary [1, 14]:
    ◦ Movement: Troops are ordered to Skêwjan(walk/march) [1, 3] to patrol the mountain borders.
    ◦ Intelligence: Officers must Witan (know/command knowledge) [1, 3] regarding the positions of the enemy.
    ◦ Logistics: Local Vojak (Slavic soldiers) [1, 3] are utilized to handle delivery (donésti) of essential supplies—such as local commodities like wood (dřevo) or beer (pivo) [15, 16]—with clarity, using Slavic prefixes to indicate completion of action [17, 18].
3. Written Records: Patrol reports and administrative record-keeping in the Grads utilize a simplified form of the Gothic script [10, 19], which remains the established, politically sanctioned writing system in the area, being centuries older than any indigenous Slavic script [10, 20].
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. THREAT ASSESSMENT AND READINESS (CERTAMINIS)
The mountain rim is the location of highest alert, focused on preventing incursions by nomadic forces and maintaining readiness against the Byzantine threat.
1. Primary Threat (Fiand): Vigilance remains focused on the great hordes of the Avars and other Asiatic fiand(enemies/foes) [3, 5, 21]. These threats necessitate the continuous organization of patrols to monitor large enemy movements (Swarms) [3].
2. Military Ethos: The continuous pressure from external gentilitas [5] imposes a necessary warlike spirit upon the Slavic populace [9], accelerating the "infusion of Gothic military ethos into the democratic... population" [22]. This aggressive posture is crucial for maintaining the bulwark [4].
3. Readiness Status: Garrisons are prepared to execute military plans and respond quickly. The legal tradition of Jus Civilitas [3, 23] demands that the Goths "observe justice and preserve laws on a sure basis" [2], applying the same high standard of organization to military preparation.
RECOMMENDATION (IMPERATIV)
All Comites are commanded to maintain strict discipline regarding the use of the Koine in military command and to ensure meticulous record-keeping (Numerus) [4, 14]. This administrative superiority is the key to achieving Sihu(Victory) [1, 3] against the enemies of the realm.
Gud miþ uns [3, 24].
(END OF REPORT)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Slavic Ascent in Bohemian Gothic Nobility
Yes, based on the internal dynamics established within the Bohemian Gothic realm, the necessities of administration and military function would have inevitably led to the rise of elite Slavic families to noble or near-noble classes within a few generations.
This rise would occur through two primary, interrelated channels: military command and economic administration, despite the Gothic aristocracy’s best efforts to maintain a rigid caste system [1].
1. Rise Through Military and Local Political Integration
The Gothic strategy for survival against external threats (like the Avars) mandated the integration and promotion of Slavic leadership, creating a path to elevated status.
• Utilization of Indigenous Leaders: The Goths recognized the need to use the "local strength of the Slavs" [2]. The established administrative strategy involved elevating the indigenous leaders, the Zupani and Knes (Slavic dignitaries), to command the Slavic Foederati [2, 3]. These leaders were already figures of local authority [4, 5].
• Shared Command and Organization: The Goths maintained their own high officers (Comites), but the external invasion imposed a military necessity that superseded the internal conflict [2, 6]. This forced cooperation required the Goths to formally recognize and utilize Slavic authority in the military hierarchy, giving the Slavic population a crucial stake in the Gothic-led defense [6].
• The Koine as the Ladder to Rank: Advancement in the military structure was tied to functional competence in the Gothic-Slavic Koine (lingua militaris), the specialized language of command and logistics [2]. Slavs who mastered the Koine—the vocabulary of order (Imperativ) and administrative necessity (Numerus) [3, 7]—would become indispensable military auxiliaries and officers, confirming that military advancement was tied to the acquisition of the state’s functional language [Previous response].
• The Infusion of Warlike Spirit: The need to fight hard against the Avars accelerated the infusion of the Gothic "warlike spirit" into the generally peaceful and industriousSlavic population [6, 8]. This injection of military ethos would legitimize the Slavic military leaders in the eyes of the Gothic warrior caste, whose culture valued valour [8].
2. Rise Through Economic and Administrative Necessity
The creation of the most sophisticated economy in the region, centered in the Grads (cities) [Previous response], required a literate, professional Slavic managerial class.
• Literate Mercantile Elite: The Slavs were designated the "trading and labouring caste," focusing on industrious activity [9, 10]. The Koine served as the indispensable market language [1, 10, 11]. Literacy in the Koine (in the Gothic script or a simplified Latinate form) was concentrated in the cities (Grads) and was required to manage commercial transactions, weights, taxes (Terna), and quotas (Numerus) [1, 9, 12, 13].
• Access to High Administration: A subset of the mercantile class involved in large-scale transactions and urban logistics would require literacy to access the legal and administrative vocabulary of the ruling elite [14]. The Gothic state, built on Roman legal traditions (Civilitas), allowed Romans (and, by extension, the subjugated population) to continue holding all the offices of the state in Italy, suggesting a legal precedent for non-Goths filling high administrative and civil roles [15].
• Wealth and Social Status: In later Slavic territories, the inhabitants of the cities constituted a primary social class alongside the nobility [9, 16]. The Slavic Koine-speaking families who controlled the commerce, logistics, and tax collection would accrue significant wealth and exert decisive influence in the organized state, leading to their eventual elevation to near-noble or noble rank based on economic power and administrative function.
Conclusion: Nobility Despite Caste Conflict
While the Gothic political structure explicitly contained the "germs of privileged castes" and fundamentally clashed with the "purely democratic" elements of the Slavs [17, 18], the need for a cohesive, effective state against formidable enemies (the Avars) and the necessity of managing the most sophisticated economy in the region provided the material and administrative means for elite Slavic families to rise.
The Goths' policy of utilizing local Slavic chiefs (Zupani and Knes) as military and administrative officers, coupled with the functional and wealth-generating Koine economy, created institutional pathways for the Slavs to acquire military glory (Sihu) and political power, leading to the creation of a new, functional nobility of Slavic origin within the Gothic realm.

       OL. CIHELKA

1935

STÁTNÍ NAKLADATELSTVÍ V PRAZE




Had


Oldřich zanesl oběd tatínkovi, který lámal „Pod skalou“ kámen. Řekl
mu, co je doma nového, ale dlouho se s ním nezdržoval. Rozběhl se
na vršek skály, odkud byl tak krásný rozhled na daleký kraj. Na jedné
straně hrad Buchlov trčel do výše jako tichý, zamlklý svědek zašlých
časů, na druhé straně ležela úrodná rovina, vroubená výběžky Bílých
Karpat. To bylo Oldřichovo zamilované místo, na němž by dovedl proseděti
celý život. Hluboko pod ním pracovali lidé. Jejich kladiva temnými údery
si vyprávěla pohádku o tvrdém životě.

Lehl si na skálu, ruce si dal pod hlavu, aby to tak netlačilo, a
díval se za malými obláčky, které pluly oblohou. Oh, kdyby se tak mohl
jednou vznésti až k obloze a dívati se se závratných výšin na zemi! Jak
malinká by byla města! A řeky! Ten jejich potok by asi vůbec nebylo
vidět. A co lidé? Rozeznal by člověka od neživého předmětu?

Sluníčko příjemně hřálo a sladká únava zavírala oči. Ostatně, však
tatínek na něj zavolá, až půjde domů. Oldřich usnul.

Jak dlouho tak ležel, nevěděl. Ale probudil ho zlý sen. Zdálo se mu,
že se setkal s jakýmsi zarostlým pobudou, který chtěl na něm peníze.
Nadarmo mu Oldřich dokazoval, že žádných nemá. Pobuda se k němu blížil,
zlé jeho oči se potměšile blýskaly a náhle povalil Oldřicha k zemi.
Dopadl na něj celou vahou svého těla. Až se mu dech zatajil. A cizinec
tlačil na jeho prsa čím dále tím prudčeji. Oldřich cítil, že to dlouho
nevydrží, že za chvilku přestane dýchat — — Vtom procitl. Slunce ještě
svítilo a Oldřich si spokojeně oddechl. Chtěl radostí zavýsknout, že
všechna ta hrůza byla jen snem, ale podivná tíha na prsou mu v tom
zabránila. Jako by tam měl nějaký balvan. Pohled jeho se svezl na hruď.

Na prsou mu ležel had. Vyšel si patrně na procházku a na měkkém
místečku se zastavil a vyhříval se. Oldřich leknutím zbledl a na čele mu
vyvstal studený pot. Co teď? Pohne-li se, had to ucítí a může uštknout.
Zůstane raději ležet nepohnutě. Ale jak dlouho to vydrží? A co, když
zakašle? Jak si pomoci z tohoto strašného postavení?

A dole, necelých sto metrů pod ním, pracuje tatínek. Oh, kdyby tak
věděl, jaké nebezpečí hrozí Oldřichovi! Jistě by okamžitě nechal
práce a spěchal nahoru zahnat nepohodlného hosta! Ale jak ho o tom
uvědomiti? Vykřiknout? Nebyla by to jistá záhuba? Jak si jen pomoci? Jak?

Minuty se vlekly nekonečně pomalu. Oldřich přimhouřenýma očima
pozoroval hada. Měl vztyčenou hlavu a volně jí otáčel. Nebylo možno
zůstati tak ležet. Celé tělo bylo otlačeno od tvrdé skály. Musí se nějak
osvobodit, a kdyby to bylo i s nasazením vlastního života. Smělý,
odvážný plán bleskl Oldřichovými myšlenkami.

Had zase otočil hlavu, takže se díval tím směrem jako Oldřich.
To byla nejpříhodnější chvíle! Oldřich se bleskurychle rozehnal, pravou
rukou uchopil zmiji těsně pod hlavou a sevřel ji tak prudce, že se mu
nehty zaryly do dlaně. Had sebou prudce smýkal v zoufalém úsilí po
svobodě, ale nadarmo. Oldřich nepustil. . .

A potom, zesláblý přestálým strachem a nebezpečím, ale s vítězným
úsměvem na tváři, spěchal za tatínkem, aby mu ukázal zabitého
nepřítele.




U stromečku


Bylo po večeři. Pět harantů sedělo za stolem s neobyčejně vážnými
tvářemi. Kdo sebou jen maličko zavrtěl, na toho dopadl přísný
pohled nejstaršího, dvanáctiletého Karla. Přišla veliká, slavná chvíle.

Tatínek již před chvílí odešel z jizby. Maminka ještě uklízela se
stolu zbytky bohaté štědrovečerní večeře. Když byla se vším hotova,
řekla:

„No, a včil buďte pěkně potichu! Dybyste dělali křik, Ježíšek by
sa u nás nezastavil.“

Vtom se ozval tichý, tlumený hlas zvonku. Děti sebou trhly.
Ježíšek už jde! Malý Joza zapištěl:

„Mami, děte mu ukázat, gde býváme! Dyby k nám tak nemohl trefit!
Otevřete vráta a postavte sa do nich s lampú, aby vás bylo zdaleka
vidět —“

„No, půjdu sa tam podívat,“ povídá matka. „Enom sa ně tu nepobijte,
lebo byste měli po radosti.“

Vyšla do síně. Děti sedí potichu, ani nedutají. Oči jsou upřeny
na dveře. A zase — slyš! Hlas zvonku se ozval jasněji, jako by to bylo
na jejich dvoře.

Kdosi klepe na dveře. Vchází maminka, za ní tatínek. Maminka drží
v ruce malý, ale cukrovím a ozdobami bohatě ověšený stromeček.

„Tak, děti, to máte za to, že ste byly hodné.“

Postavila jej na stůl.

„Jéjdanečky, ten je pěkný!“ vykřikuje Joza.

Klima tahá tatínka za kabát.

„Tati, toť je voják a má aj flintu!“

„Panečku, to Valentovi istě nebudú mět takový jako my!“ rozumuje
Mařka.

„Jak to možeš vědět?“ ptá se matka.

„Dyž jejich Lida sa s každým enom hádá —“

„A hen, hen,“ Tonek ukazuje vzrušeně na horní větévku, „Karle,
podívaj sa, vidíš ho?“

„Co? Co?“ všichni se zvědavě dívají na místo, kam ukazuje.

„No teho koníčka. . . páni, celý z čokolády!“ Nemůže tomu ani
uvěřiti.

Opravdu! Na silné větévce se houpal čokoládový koník, veliký
skoro jako pěst.

„Ten by stál aspoň tisíc korun!“ rozumuje Joza. Školáci —
Karel, Mařka a Tonek — se dávají do smíchu.

„Ty tomu rozumíš!“

Prohlížejí stromeček se všech stran. Ne, takové krásy ještě
neviděli! A ten kůň, Bože, ten čokoládový kůň! Kdyby jich tam bylo
aspoň pět takových! Vždyť jak se o něj rozdělí?

Karel se tajemně usmíval. Vždyť už ví, jak to udělá: sám si nechá
břicho a hlavu. Ostatní podělí tak, že na každého se dostane jedna
noha. Ale křik bude, to je jisté. Zvláště až Joza spustí!

„Ale to vám povídám,“ napomínal otec, „do Třech králů sa nesmí
utrhnút ani jeden kúsek. Jináč byste už po druhéj stromku nedostali!“

Konečně byl čas ke spaní.

Nějak se jim dnes nechtělo.

V celé jizbě měli jenom dvě postele. Proto Karel spával na zemi,
Tonek na lávce a Mařka za stolem.

A kdyby jej dostal on celého, pěkně by si jej schoval do sotora a ani by

PROCOPIUS OF CAESAREA

HISTORY OF THE WARS.

BOOK III

THE VANDALIC WAR


I

Such, then, was the final outcome of the Persian War for the Emperor
Justinian; and I shall now proceed to set forth all that he did against
the Vandals and the Moors. But first shall be told whence came the host
of the Vandals when they descended upon the land of the Romans. After
Theodosius, the Roman Emperor, had departed from the world, having
proved himself one of the most just of men and an able warrior, his
kingdom was taken over by his two sons, Arcadius, the elder, receiving
the Eastern portion, and Honorius, the younger, the Western. [Jan. 17,
395 A.D.] But the Roman power had been thus divided as far back as the
time of Constantine and his sons; for he transferred his government to
Byzantium, and making the city larger and much more renowned, allowed it
to be named after him.

Now the earth is surrounded by a circle of ocean, either entirely or for
the most part (for our knowledge is not as yet at all clear in this
matter); and it is split into two continents by a sort of outflow from
the ocean, a flow which enters at the western part and forms this Sea
which we know, beginning at Gadira[1] and extending all the way to the
Maeotic Lake.[2] Of these two continents the one to the right, as one
sails into the Sea, as far as the Lake, has received the name of Asia,
beginning at Gadira and at the southern[3] of the two Pillars of
Heracles. Septem[4] is the name given by the natives to the fort at that
point, since seven hills appear there; for "septem" has the force of
"seven" in the Latin tongue. And the whole continent opposite this was
named Europe. And the strait at that point separates the two
continents[5] by about eighty-four stades, but from there on they are
kept apart by wide expanses of sea as far as the Hellespont. For at this
point they again approach each other at Sestus and Abydus, and once more
at Byzantium and Chalcedon as far as the rocks called in ancient times
the "Dark Blue Rocks," where even now is the place called Hieron. For at
these places the continents are separated from one another by a distance
of only ten stades and even less than that.

Now the distance from one of the Pillars of Heracles to the other, if
one goes along the shore and does not pass around the Ionian Gulf and
the sea called the Euxine but crosses from Chalcedon[6] to Byzantium and
from Dryous[7] to the opposite mainland,[8] is a journey of two hundred
and eighty-five days for an unencumbered traveller. For as to the land
about the Euxine Sea, which extends from Byzantium to the Lake, it would
be impossible to tell everything with precision, since the barbarians
beyond the Ister River, which they also call the Danube, make the shore
of that sea quite impossible for the Romans to traverse--except, indeed,
that from Byzantium to the mouth of the Ister is a journey of twenty-two
days, which should be added to the measure of Europe by one making the
computation. And on the Asiatic side, that is from Chalcedon to the
Phasis River, which, flowing from the country of the Colchians, descends
into the Pontus, the journey is accomplished in forty days. So that the
whole Roman domain, according to the distance along the sea at least,
attains the measure of a three hundred and forty-seven days' journey,
if, as has been said, one ferries over the Ionian Gulf, which extends
about eight hundred stades from Dryous. For the passage across the
gulf[9] amounts to a journey of not less than four days. Such, then, was
the size of the Roman empire in the ancient times.

And there fell to him who held the power in the West the most of Libya,
extending ninety days' journey--for such is the distance from Gadira to
the boundaries of Tripolis in Libya; and in Europe he received as his
portion territory extending seventy-five days' journey--for such is the
distance from the northern[10] of the Pillars of Heracles to the Ionian
Gulf.[11] And one might add also the distance around the gulf. And the
emperor of the East received territory extending one hundred and twenty
days' journey, from the boundaries of Cyrene in Libya as far as
Epidamnus, which lies on the Ionian Gulf and is called at the present
time Dyrrachium, as well as that portion of the country about the Euxine
Sea which, as previously stated, is subject to the Romans. Now one day's
journey extends two hundred and ten stades,[12] or as far as from Athens
to Megara. Thus, then, the Roman emperors divided either continent
between them. And among the islands Britain, which is outside the
Pillars of Heracles and by far the largest of all islands, was counted,
as is natural, with the West; and inside the Pillars, Ebusa,[13] which
lies in the Mediterranean in what we may call the Propontis, just inside
the opening where the ocean enters, about seven days' journey from the
opening, and two others near it, Majorica and Minorica, as they are
called by the natives, were also assigned to the Western empire. And
each of the islands in the Sea itself fell to the share of that one of
the two emperors within whose boundaries it happened to lie.


II

Now while Honorius was holding the imperial power in the West,
barbarians took possession of his land; and I shall tell who they were
and in what manner they did so. [395-423 A.D.] There were many Gothic
nations in earlier times, just as also at the present, but the greatest
and most important of all are the Goths, Vandals, Visigoths, and
Gepaedes. In ancient times, however, they were named Sauromatae and
Melanchlaeni;[14] and there were some too who called these nations
Getic. All these, while they are distinguished from one another by their
names, as has been said, do not differ in anything else at all. For they
all have white bodies and fair hair, and are tall and handsome to look
upon, and they use the same laws and practise a common religion. For
they are all of the Arian faith, and have one language called Gothic;
and, as it seems to me, they all came originally from one tribe, and
were distinguished later by the names of those who led each group. This
people used to dwell above the Ister River from of old. Later on the
Gepaedes got possession of the country about Singidunum[15] and
Sirmium,[16] on both sides of the Ister River, where they have remained
settled even down to my time.

But the Visigoths, separating from the others, removed from there and at
first entered into an alliance with the Emperor Arcadius, but at a later
time (for faith with the Romans cannot dwell in barbarians), under the
leadership of Alaric, they became hostile to both emperors, and,
beginning with Thrace, treated all Europe as an enemy's land. Now the
Emperor Honorius had before this time been sitting in Rome, with never a
thought of war in his mind, but glad, I think, if men allowed him to
remain quiet in his palace. But when word was brought that the
barbarians with a great army were not far off, but somewhere among the
Taulantii,[17] he abandoned the palace and fled in disorderly fashion to
Ravenna, a strong city lying just about at the end of the Ionian Gulf,
while some say that he brought in the barbarians himself, because an
uprising had been started against him among his subjects; but this does
not seem to me trustworthy, as far, at least, as one can judge of the
character of the man. And the barbarians, finding that they had no
hostile force to encounter them, became the most cruel of all men. For
they destroyed all the cities which they captured, especially those
south of the Ionian Gulf, so completely that nothing has been left to my
time to know them by, unless, indeed, it might be one tower or one gate
or some such thing which chanced to remain. And they killed all the
people, as many as came in their way, both old and young alike, sparing
neither women nor children. Wherefore even up to the present time Italy
is sparsely populated. They also gathered as plunder all the money out
of all Europe, and, most important of all, they left in Rome nothing
whatever of public or private wealth when they moved on to Gaul. But I
shall now tell how Alaric captured Rome.

After much time had been spent by him in the siege, and he had not been
able either by force or by any other device to capture the place, he
formed the following plan. Among the youths in the army whose beards had
not yet grown, but who had just come of age, he chose out three hundred
whom he knew to be of good birth and possessed of valour beyond their
years, and told them secretly that he was about to make a present of
them to certain of the patricians in Rome, pretending that they were
slaves. And he instructed them that, as soon as they got inside the
houses of those men, they should display much gentleness and moderation
and serve them eagerly in whatever tasks should be laid upon them by
their owners; and he further directed them that not long afterwards, on
an appointed day at about midday, when all those who were to be their
masters would most likely be already asleep after their meal, they
should all come to the gate called Salarian and with a sudden rush kill
the guards, who would have no previous knowledge of the plot, and open
the gates as quickly as possible. After giving these orders to the
youths, Alaric straightway sent ambassadors to the members of the
senate, stating that he admired them for their loyalty toward their
emperor, and that he would trouble them no longer, because of their
valour and faithfulness, with which it was plain that they were endowed
to a remarkable degree, and in order that tokens of himself might be
preserved among men both noble and brave, he wished to present each one
of them with some domestics. After making this declaration and sending
the youths not long afterwards, he commanded the barbarians to make
preparations for the departure, and he let this be known to the Romans.
And they heard his words gladly, and receiving the gifts began to be
exceedingly happy, since they were completely ignorant of the plot of
the barbarian. For the youths, by being unusually obedient to their
owners, averted suspicion, and in the camp some were already seen moving
from their positions and raising the siege, while it seemed that the
others were just on the point of doing the very same thing. But when the
appointed day had come, Alaric armed his whole force for the attack and
was holding them in readiness close by the Salarian Gate; for it
happened that he had encamped there at the beginning of the siege. And
all the youths at the time of the day agreed upon came to this gate,
and, assailing the guards suddenly, put them to death; then they opened
the gates and received Alaric and the army into the city at their
leisure. [Aug. 24, 410 A.D.] And they set fire to the houses which were
next to the gate, among which was also the house of Sallust, who in
ancient times wrote the history of the Romans, and the greater part of
this house has stood half-burned up to my time; and after plundering the
whole city and destroying the most of the Romans, they moved on. At that
time they say that the Emperor Honorius in Ravenna received the message
from one of the eunuchs, evidently a keeper of the poultry, that Rome
had perished. And he cried out and said, "And yet it has just eaten from
my hands!" For he had a very large cock, Rome by name; and the eunuch
comprehending his words said that it was the city of Rome which had
perished at the hands of Alaric, and the emperor with a sigh of relief
answered quickly: "But I, my good fellow, thought that my fowl Rome had
perished." So great, they say, was the folly with which this emperor was
possessed.

But some say that Rome was not captured in this way by Alaric, but that
Proba, a woman of very unusual eminence in wealth and in fame among the
Roman senatorial class, felt pity for the Romans who were being
destroyed by hunger and the other suffering they endured; for they were
already even tasting each other's flesh; and seeing that every good hope
had left them, since both the river and the harbour were held by the
enemy, she commanded her domestics, they say, to open the gates by
night.

Now when Alaric was about to depart from Rome, he declared Attalus, one
of their nobles, emperor of the Romans, investing him with the diadem
and the purple and whatever else pertains to the imperial dignity. And
he did this with the intention of removing Honorius from his throne and
of giving over the whole power in the West to Attalus. With such a
purpose, then, both Attalus and Alaric were going with a great army
against Ravenna. But this Attalus was neither able to think wisely
himself, nor to be persuaded by one who had wisdom to offer. So while
Alaric did not by any means approve the plan, Attalus sent commanders to
Libya without an army. Thus, then, were these things going on.

And the island of Britain revolted from the Romans, and the soldiers
there chose as their king Constantinus, a man of no mean station. [407
A.D.] And he straightway gathered a fleet of ships and a formidable army
and invaded both Spain and Gaul with a great force, thinking to enslave
these countries. But Honorius was holding ships in readiness and waiting
to see what would happen in Libya, in order that, if those sent by
Attalus were repulsed, he might himself sail for Libya and keep some
portion of his own kingdom, while if matters there should go against
him, he might reach Theodosius and remain with him. For Arcadius had
already died long before, and his son Theodosius, still a very young
child,[18] held the power of the East. [408-450 A.D.] But while Honorius
was thus anxiously awaiting the outcome of these events and tossed amid
the billows of uncertain fortune, it so chanced that some wonderful
pieces of good fortune befell him. For God is accustomed to succour
those who are neither clever nor able to devise anything of themselves,
and to lend them assistance, if they be not wicked, when they are in the
last extremity of despair; such a thing, indeed, befell this emperor.
For it was suddenly reported from Libya that the commanders of Attalus
had been destroyed, and that a host of ships was at hand from Byzantium
with a very great number of soldiers who had come to assist him, though
he had not expected them, and that Alaric, having quarrelled with
Attalus, had stripped him of the emperor's garb and was now keeping him
under guard in the position of a private citizen. [411 A.D.] And
afterwards Alaric died of disease, and the army of the Visigoths under
the leadership of Adaulphus proceeded into Gaul, and Constantinus,
defeated in battle, died with his sons. However the Romans never
succeeded in recovering Britain, but it remained from that time on under
tyrants. And the Goths, after making the crossing of the Ister, at first
occupied Pannonia, but afterwards, since the emperor gave them the
right, they inhabited the country of Thrace. And after spending no great
time there they conquered the West. But this will be told in the
narrative concerning the Goths.


III

Now the Vandals dwelling about the Maeotic Lake, since they were pressed
by hunger, moved to the country of the Germans, who are now called
Franks, and the river Rhine, associating with themselves the Alani, a
Gothic people. Then from there, under the leadership of Godigisclus,
they moved and settled in Spain, which is the first land of the Roman
empire on the side of the ocean. At that time Honorius made an agreement
with Godigisclus that they should settle there on condition that it
should not be to the detriment of the country. But there was a law among
the Romans, that if any persons should fail to keep their property in
their own possession, and if, meanwhile, a time amounting to thirty
years should pass, that these persons should thenceforth not be entitled
to proceed against those who had forced them out, but they were excluded
by demurrer[19] from access to the court; and in view of this he
established a law that whatever time should be spent by the Vandals in
the Roman domain should not by any means be counted toward this
thirty-year demurrer. And Honorius himself, when the West had been
driven by him to this pass, died of disease. [Aug. 27, 423 A.D.] Now
before this, as it happened, the royal power had been shared by Honorius
with Constantius, the husband of Placidia, the sister of Arcadius and
Honorius; but he lived to exercise the power only a few days, and then,
becoming seriously ill, he died while Honorius was still living, [421
A.D.] having never succeeded in saying or in doing anything worth
recounting; for the time was not sufficient during which he lived in
possession of the royal power. Now a son of this Constantius,
Valentinian, a child just weaned, was being reared in the palace of
Theodosius, but the members of the imperial court in Rome chose one of
the soldiers there, John by name, as emperor. This man was both gentle
and well-endowed with sagacity and thoroughly capable of valorous deeds.
At any rate he held the tyranny five years[20] and directed it with
moderation, and he neither gave ear to slanderers nor did he do any
unjust murder, willingly at least, nor did he set his hand to robbing
men of money; but he did not prove able to do anything at all against
the barbarians, since his relations with Byzantium were hostile. Against
this John, Theodosius, the son of Arcadius, sent a great army and Aspar
and Ardaburius, the son of Aspar, as generals, and wrested from him the
tyranny and gave over the royal power to Valentinian, who was still a
child. And Valentinian took John alive, and he brought him out in the
hippodrome of Aquileia with one of his hands cut off and caused him to
ride in state on an ass, and then after he had suffered much ill
treatment from the stage-performers there, both in word and in deed, he
put him to death. [426 A.D.] Thus Valentinian took over the power of the
West. But Placidia, his mother, had reared this emperor and educated him
in an altogether effeminate manner, and in consequence he was filled
with wickedness from childhood. For he associated mostly with sorcerers
and those who busy themselves with the stars, and, being an
extraordinarily zealous pursuer of love affairs with other men's wives,
he conducted himself in a most indecent manner, although he was married
to a woman of exceptional beauty. [455 A.D.] And not only was this true,
but he also failed to recover for the empire anything of what had been
wrested from it before, and he both lost Libya in addition to the
territory previously lost and was himself destroyed. And when he
perished, it fell to the lot of his wife and his children to become
captives. Now the disaster in Libya came about as follows.

There were two Roman generals, Aetius and Boniface, especially valiant
men and in experience of many wars inferior to none of that time at
least. These two came to be at variance in regard to matters of state,
but they attained to such a degree of highmindedness and excellence in
every respect that if one should call either of them "the last of the
Romans" he would not err, so true was it that all the excellent
qualities of the Romans were summed up in these two men. One of these,
Boniface, was appointed by Placidia general of all Libya. Now this was
not in accord with the wishes of Aetius, but he by no means disclosed
the fact that it did not please him. For their hostility had not as yet
come to light, but was concealed behind the countenance of each. But
when Boniface had got out of the way, Aetius slandered him to Placidia,
saying that he was setting up a tyranny and had robbed her and the
emperor of all Libya, and he said that it was very easy for her to find
out the truth; for if she should summon Boniface to Rome, he would never
come. And when the woman heard this, Aetius seemed to her to speak well
and she acted accordingly. But Aetius, anticipating her, wrote to
Boniface secretly that the mother of the emperor was plotting against

                     JAROSLAV VICTOR NIGRIN, A. M.
               HARRISON TECHNICAL HIGH SCHOOL, CHICAGO.

                            [Illustration]

                  BOHEMIAN LITERARY SOCIETY. CHICAGO.
